claims.text: Monte Carlo-generated chemical short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr forms HfTi and TiZr binary clusters.
The HfTi and TiZr clusters organize into percolative, B2-like networks.
B2-like binary ordering reduces the root-mean-square lattice distortion relative to a random HfNbTaTiZr solid solution.
Reduced lattice distortion shifts the high-frequency phonon density of states toward higher frequencies.
The high-frequency DOS shift increases phonon group velocity.
B2-like ordering produces a net increase in lattice thermal conductivity relative to the random solid solution.
The initial equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr random solid solution has significant local lattice distortion caused by atomic-size mismatch.
Thermal annealing or rapid quenching can favor percolative HfTi and TiZr SRO without producing macroscopic precipitates.
Chemical SRO is stable and diffusion remains active in HfNbTaTiZr over 800–1200 K.
Percolating B2-like clusters act as phonon highways by locally relaxing strain.
Ordering reduces the local variance in atomic size and bonding environment.
Reduced distortion lowers the scattering cross-section of high-frequency phonons.
Continuous cluster pathways give high-frequency phonons lower scattering rates and longer mean free paths.
The ordered state will have reduced Debye-Waller factors for the cluster-forming elements.
AlCoFeNi-based alloys can separate into distinct B2 and BCC phases after annealing or Cr substitution.
Isolated precipitates or B2/BCC phase separation with a high interfacial density decrease thermal conductivity through interface scattering.
Multiphase AlCoCrFeNi alloys under irradiation exhibit a conductivity decrease analogous to the proposed interface-dominated regime.
A lower conductivity, or a broadened or downward-shifted high-frequency DOS in the ordered sample, would falsify the proposed mechanism.
